item.title: In pictures: Partial to total eclipse sweeps across much of Europe
item.description: The total eclipse in Spain – and partial eclipse seen across much of Europe – gave rise to a host of incredible photos.

item.title: The moment of the total solar eclipse in Spain
item.description: This is the moment a total solar eclipse took place over northern Spain on Wednesday evening.

item.title: Netanyahu gave a ‘victory to Hamas’ by rejecting US-backed Gaza peace plan
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s rejection of a US-backed peace plan for Gaza last week offered a diplomatic victory to Hamas, according to some analysts. The Palestinian Islamist movement had agreed to gradually give up weapons in exchange for an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza, but agreeing on the definition of "disarmament" may prove a sticking point.
item.dc:creator: Grégoire SAUVAGE

item.title: Voting ends in US midwest primaries
item.description: Voters in six US states went to the polls to choose their preferred candidates in primaries and special elections ahead of November’s midterms. In Wisconsin, moderate David Crowley narrowly defeated Democratic socialist Francesca Hong in the race for governor. On the Republican side, Darline Graham, sister of the late Senator Lindsey Graham, advanced to a runoff in the Senate primary. Yuka Royer has the story.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Lebanon becomes first Middle East country to end death penalty
item.description: Lebanon’s parliament voted on Tuesday to abolish the death penalty, making the country the first in the Middle East to do so. Lebanon has not carried out an execution since 2004, but death sentences have continued to be handed down, with the latest issued on Monday. Amnesty International says at least 85 people were still on death row as of January this year. Capital punishment in Lebanon has typically applied to serious crimes including murder, terrorism and espionage. France 24 correspondent Renée Davis reports the latest from Beirut.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Colombia: Bogota's search for survivors continues
item.description: The search for survivors continues in Colombia, more than 48 hours after a 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck the country. More than 200 people have been confirmed dead, while more than 2,000 are reported missing. The new president, Abelardo de la Espriella, has declared a state of emergency, as many people remain without clean drinking water or electricity and several major highways are still closed. Carys Garland’s report begins with the dramatic rescue of a man from the wreckage of his home.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Israeli troops fail to remove settlers besieging Palestinian homes in West Bank village
item.description: The Israeli military on Wednesday failed to remove settlers from blockaded Palestinian homes in the occupied West Bank. The siege began over the weekend, when a group of settlers blocked essential supplies from entering the Palestinian village of Qusra. The incident marked a ⁠rare confrontation between settlers and the Israeli military.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Spain prepares for rare total solar eclipse
item.description: We’re just hours away from a rare total solar eclipse, with parts of northern Spain set to briefly turn from day to night as the Moon blocks out the Sun. Millions more will see a partial eclipse across Europe, Canada, the northern US and northwest Africa. But beyond the spectacle, eclipses also offer scientists valuable insights into the Sun and our universe. France 24 correspondent Sarah Morris reports from Segovia, Spain.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Putin threatens to seize European ships
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has threatened retaliation over the West’s seizure of commercial vessels. Speaking aboard a Russian warship, Putin described the measures targeting Russia as an act of piracy and robbery. France 24 International Affairs editor Philip Turle shares further insights.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Meta faces $1.4 trillion lawsuit
item.description: Mark Zuckerberg’s tech giant Meta is facing a $1.4 trillion lawsuit over allegations that it deliberately designed addictive features on its platforms to keep children hooked. Parents have long raised concerns about the impact of Facebook and Instagram on young people’s mental health, and jury selection begins this Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Colombia: Woman rescued from under earthquake debris after 36 hours
item.description:
🇨🇴 A woman trapped under the debris of a collapsed hotel in Pereira, #Colombia, was rescued on Tuesday after spending 36 hours under the rubble.
Search and rescue operations are still underway in the country's coffee-growing Chocó region which was at the epîcentre of a 7.4 magnitude #earthquake on Monday.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Colombia declares three days of mourning as search for quake survivors continues
item.description: Colombia on Wednesday declared three days of mourning after a 7.4-magnitude earthquake killed more than 200 people in the west of the country. Monday's quake was the strongest to hit Colombia this century, and the search for survivors under the rubble is ongoing.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Faced with ageing population, Vietnam seeks to curb falling birthrate
item.description: Vietnam, a country of more than 100 million people, is facing a sharp decline in its birthrate. Once known for large families, the nation's fertility rate has fallen to just 1.9 children per woman. This figure worries the government, which for decades was obsessed with controlling population growth. For more than 40 years, a two-child policy was the norm in Vietnam – a restriction that was only lifted in June 2025.
item.dc:creator: Dung Vo Trung

item.title: Lebanese parliament passes sweeping amnesty law to reduce overcrowding in prisons
item.description: Lebanon's parliament on Wednesday passed a general amnesty law reducing sentences for inmates and people detained for more than 12 years without charges in a bid to reduce prison overcrowding. The legislation was passed a day after Lebanon became the first Middle Eastern country to abolish the death penalty.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Parts of Spain plunged into darkness as eclipse moves across Europe
item.description: Parts of Spain were briefly plunged into darkness on Wednesday as a solar eclipse that began in Iceland and the Arctic progressed across the continent. It was the first total eclipse to be seen from mainland Europe in two decades. Read our blog to see how the event unfolded.
item.dc:creator: Simon FEISTHAUER FOURNET

item.title: What can we learn from eclipses?
item.description: A total solar eclipse will sweep across northern Spain on August 12 in one of Europe's most anticipated astronomical events of the decade. From the Sun's corona to animal behaviour and human emotions, these rare celestial events continue to provide scientists with valuable insights more than two millennia after they were first observed. Head of Space Science at the Centre National d'Études Spatiales, Olivier Joie-La Marle, shares further insights.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Solar eclipse: A rare show that reveals scientific secrets
item.description: Parts of northern Spain are set to turn from day to night as the Moon blocks out the Sun. Millions more will see a partial eclipse across Europe, Canada, the northern US and northwest Africa. But beyond the spectacle, eclipses also offer scientists valuable insights into the Sun and our universe. Ellen Gainsford has more.

item.title: Ukraine seeks closer cooperation with South Korea
item.description: Earlier this week, Zelenskyy accused North Korea of stepping up its support for Russia, with ballistic missiles from Pyongyang reportedly used in another deadly attack on Zaporizhzhia. Let’s get more on this from France 24’s correspondent in South Korea, Chloe Borgnon.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Meta group is accused of intentionally designing addictive platforms
item.description:
$1.4 trillion in fines… That’s the astronomical sum four US states are seeking from Meta, the company founded by Mark Zuckerberg.
California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey accuse the company of deliberately making Instagram and Facebook addictive for minors.
Wassim Cornet reports from Los Angeles.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Solar eclipse: "Never look at it without eye protection"
item.description: We’re just hours away from a rare celestial event, a total solar eclipse. Day will briefly turn into night across parts of northern Spain as the Moon completely blocks out the Sun. Beyond Spain, millions more will see a partial eclipse across Europe, Canada, the northern US and northwest Africa. And we’ll have plenty of coverage for you throughout the day. Francis Monte reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Meta faces new high-stakes trial
item.description: It’s being described as social media’s “Big Tobacco moment”, with a major trial against Meta opening today. Mark Zuckerberg’s company is defending itself against allegations that it harmed children by designing addictive features for young users on Instagram and Facebook. France 24 journalist Delano D'Souza shares further insights.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Millions gear up for first total eclipse since 2006
item.description: A total solar eclipse will sweep across northern Spain on August 12 in one of Europe's most anticipated astronomical events of the decade. From the Sun's corona to animal behaviour and human emotions, these rare celestial events continue to provide scientists with valuable insights more than two millennia after they were first observed. Selina Sykes reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Key US primary races take shape
item.description: Tuesday was primary election day in six US states, with both major parties holding runoffs in several races. In Minnesota, the progressive Lieutenant Governor defeated Representative Angie Craig in the Democratic Senate primary, while Wisconsin’s Republican gubernatorial primary remains too close to call. Also in Minnesota, eccentric Donald Trump-endorsed businessman Mike Lindell lost the Republican governor’s primary to House Speaker Lisa Demuth. And in South Carolina, Darlene Graham advanced to the Republican Senate runoff to succeed her late brother, Lindsay Graham, who died suddenly last month. France 24 International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani shares further insights.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
